root_cause_label: Misidentification of Ray-Traced 3D Scene as 2D Gradient
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent analyzed raw PPM pixel values and concluded the image was a simple 2D vertical gradient with a checkerboard, never recognizing it was a 3D ray-traced scene requiring a ray tracer implementation, and spent the remaining 116 steps fitting increasingly refined but fundamentally wrong 2D mathematical formulas.
t_err_evidence: cat > image.c with vertical-only gradient, ignoring horizontal variation in original image
t_commit_evidence: At step 19 the agent writes the first image.c based entirely on the 2D gradient premise and immediately compiles it; all 116 subsequent steps refine this wrong approach without questioning the fundamental strategy.
trigger_explanation: The agent made an unverified assumption that examining raw pixel values by sampling sparse positions in the PPM file was sufficient to understand the generative process. It observed the sky gradient (which is a natural output of a ray-traced scene with a sky background) and the checkerboard floor (viewed at an angle from a 3D camera), and incorrectly concluded these were simple 2D horizontal gradients and a per-pixel checkerboard, acting on this false premise without verifying it against the task name ('path-tracing') or any 3D interpretation.
